children: Shares of Palo Alto Networks (PANW, Financials) tumbled Friday after Bernstein downgraded the cybersecurity company to Market Perform from Outperform, citing high valuations in the sector.

Bernstein analyst Peter Weed upgraded the price target to $351 from $253, albeit the new target was still below the stock's previous trading level. Cybersecurity stocks have already priced in much of the predicted growth after rallying about 100% since early 2026, the firm said.
Adding to the selling impetus was a revelation that a director of the company sold shares at around $377 a share. PANW hit an intraday low of $359.07 compared to a 52-week high of $398.88.
The larger cybersecurity industry continues to be on a wave of increased demand for AI-related security investment. But Friday's selloff shows the risk of valuation after the sector's steep run-up.
The challenge for investors is whether Palo Alto Networks can expand earnings and cash flow fast enough to justify its lofty price.

title: Palo Alto Networks' 100% Rally Hits a Valuation Roadblock
